summary: Crown Point Light, Lake Champlain: a 1858 stone light, rebuilt as the Champlain Memorial in 1912, its light moved to a steel tower in 1926.

structures.type: octagonal masonry tower with wooden cottage
memorial tower: Doric columns and lantern around the 1858 core
steel skeleton tower with acetylene light (moved to Windmill Point in 1931)

access.note: Grounds and campground open; reached from the New York side of the Lake Champlain bridge. The U.S. Lighthouse Society archive lists it as not open to the public; LighthouseFriends reports the tower open in season.

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Naval Lieutenant Charles T. Platt recommends lights at Windmill Point and Crown Point
Congress provides $8,000 for the lighthouse (3 August 1854); title to the site takes years to settle
Octagonal stone tower and wooden cottage built by Ellis and O'Neal of Malone and Champlain
Light first shown, according to the U.S. Lighthouse Society record and Putnam (LighthouseFriends says 1859)
LighthouseFriends: fifth-order lens first shown at the opening of navigation in 1859
Keeper James Raine's two daughters drown after the ice breaks under their sleigh on Lake Champlain (18 March 1868)
Congress appropriates $1,500 for repairs; a barn is built and the dwelling repaired
Lighthouse Board: survey of the reservation and minor repairs
Tower rebuilt as the Champlain Memorial; the light established on 7 August 1912 (LighthouseFriends)
Fixed fifth-order light atop the memorial, established 7 August 1912
Efficiency flag for 1919, Third District, awarded to Crown Point (keeper Jesse Orton)
Memorial light discontinued; navigation passes to a steel skeleton tower with an acetylene light
Reservation turned over to the State of New York after Keeper Brown's retirement on 31 July 1926
Skeleton tower moved to Windmill Point to help against liquor smuggling
Lighthouse restoration completed in time for the 2009 Champlain quadricentennial, after 2004 state funding

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The U.S. Lighthouse Society record and Putnam give 1858 for the first light. LighthouseFriends says the fifth-order lens first shone at the opening of navigation in 1859. The record's first_lit 1858 follows the earlier date; the 1859 date is kept as LighthouseFriends' account.
The U.S. Lighthouse Society record says granite; LighthouseFriends says blue limestone from a subcontractor. The record's 'stone' covers both.

The U.S. Lighthouse Society record says the station is not open to the public; LighthouseFriends reports the grounds open and the tower open in season. The story gives both and advises a check before a visit.
The U.S. Lighthouse Society record gives 85 ft above water (25.9 m, the record's figure). LighthouseFriends gives 83 ft for 1859 and 89 ft after the 1912 memorial light.

notes_for_editor: Keeper roster: the eleven USLHS lines are copied as printed, with person slugs from roster.py. Catherine Brown is added from LighthouseFriends (the roster does not list her). Two different 1858 and 1859 first-light dates appear; the story gives both. Access conflict: the USLHS record says 'Open to Public: No' while LighthouseFriends says the grounds are open and the tower open in season; check with the campground or NYS DEC before a visit guide is published. The 1868 accident rests on the Worcester Daily Spy dispatch (read) and LighthouseFriends' names and ages; the New York Herald item that LighthouseFriends cites was not read. The 1925 incident rests on LighthouseFriends only. Pre-1891 Light-House Board reports are not in the local corpus, so the 1838, 1854 and 1872 facts rest on LighthouseFriends. Putnam's p. 161 comes from the printed index; the scan page is 216. The Bulletin's p. 137 donation entry is cited from the 1924-1929 index; the matching volume page was not located. The Wikipedia article was read only for leads and is not cited. The corpus's 'Crown Point, N.Y.' life-saving awards (Hiram Dudley Buck, Crown Point Center) concern a different place and are excluded. Newspaper search for the 1912 memorial found Champlain Memorial reports in the New-York Tribune (22 April 1912), The Sun (27 April 1912) and The Evening World (3 May 1912, the French bust at Crown Point), but the OCR is too damaged to quote reliably, so they are not cited; the memorial's construction and dedication rest on Putnam and LighthouseFriends. A Taft-dedication search returned unrelated Crown Point hits in other states. Fact-check 2026-10-28: Jesse Orton's name was matched by row in the OCR of the 1920 Bulletin p. 18 efficiency-flag table (third district, Crown Point, N. Y.); the page image was viewed and confirms the row. The 1893 Light-House Board entry is on printed p. 64 (the archive's OCR index lists Crown Point at p. 64; the page header reads 64) and scan p. 71; the scan-page URL is the one corpus.py prints. The 1868 dispatch is dated 19 March and says 'yesterday afternoon', which places the accident on 18 March. Under the 'Storms' heading the story quotes the dispatch's first sentence only; the rest of it is paraphrased.
